code.note: The highlighted line is the one behind the current step. The sample is tested against the animation, so they always agree.

bubble-sort.ready: Ready. Each pass carries the biggest unsorted value to the end. Press Play, or step one move at a time.
bubble-sort.compare_bigger: Is {{a}} bigger than {{b}}? Yes, so they swap.
bubble-sort.compare_ok: Is {{a}} bigger than {{b}}? No, they stay.
bubble-sort.swap: Swap {{a}} and {{b}}: {{a}} moves one place right.
bubble-sort.settled: End of the pass: {{value}} is in its final place at position {{end}}.
bubble-sort.no_swaps: No swaps in this pass, so the array is sorted: stop early.
bubble-sort.done: Sorted: {{comparisons}} comparisons and {{moves}} swaps for {{n}} values.

insertion-sort.ready: Ready. The left part grows sorted, one value at a time. Press Play, or step one move at a time.
insertion-sort.take: Lift {{key}} out of position {{i}} as the key; its place becomes the gap.
insertion-sort.compare_bigger: Is {{value}} bigger than the key {{key}}? Yes, so it shifts right.
insertion-sort.compare_stop: Is {{value}} bigger than the key {{key}}? No, so the key goes right after it.
insertion-sort.shift: Shift {{value}} right into position {{to}}; the gap moves left.
insertion-sort.insert: Drop the key {{key}} into the gap at position {{at}}.
insertion-sort.done: Sorted: {{comparisons}} comparisons and {{moves}} shifts for {{n}} values.

quick-sort.ready: Ready. Press Play, or step through one move at a time.
quick-sort.base: The range [{{lo}}..{{lo}}] holds one value, so it is already in place.
quick-sort.pivot: Partition [{{lo}}..{{hi}}]. The pivot is the last value: {{pivot}}.
quick-sort.compare_smaller: Is {{value}} smaller than {{pivot}}? Yes, it belongs in the left part.
quick-sort.compare_not: Is {{value}} smaller than {{pivot}}? No, it stays on the right.
quick-sort.swap: Swap {{value}} into position {{i}}. The left part now ends at index {{i}}.
quick-sort.swap_self: {{value}} is already at the edge of the left part, so i just moves on.
quick-sort.place: Put the pivot {{pivot}} at index {{i}}. Everything to its left is smaller; it is now in its final place.
quick-sort.done: Sorted: {{comparisons}} comparisons and {{moves}} swaps for {{n}} values.

big-o-growth.ready: Six loops, one input: n = {{n}}. Each loop counts its own steps; watch how far apart the counts end up.
big-o-growth.constant: O(1): one step, however big n is.
big-o-growth.log: i = {{i}} ≤ {{n}}, so count a step ({{steps}} so far) and double i to {{next}}.
big-o-growth.log_done: i passed n after {{steps}} doublings: O(log n). Doubling reaches n in very few steps.
big-o-growth.linear: O(n): one step per value, {{steps}} steps for n = {{n}}.
big-o-growth.nlogn: O(n log n): a doubling loop inside a loop over n: {{n}} × {{log}} = {{steps}} steps.
big-o-growth.quadratic: O(n²): one step for every pair (i, j): {{n}} × {{n}} = {{steps}} steps.
big-o-growth.exponential: O(2ⁿ): one step per subset of n items: {{steps}} steps. Each extra item doubles the work.
big-o-growth.done: At n = {{n}} the counts run from {{fastest}} to {{slowest}}. Move the n slider to compare the curves at any n.

recursion-call-stack.ready: Sum {{n}} values by recursion: the call for a range adds up the sums of its two halves.
recursion-call-stack.call: Call total({{lo}}, {{hi}}): a new frame goes on the stack (depth {{depth}}). More than one value, so it must split.
recursion-call-stack.check_leaf: Call total({{lo}}, {{hi}}): a new frame goes on the stack (depth {{depth}}). One value: this is the base case.
recursion-call-stack.leaf: Base case: return a[{{at}}] = {{value}}. The frame pops and its caller resumes.
recursion-call-stack.split: mid = {{mid}}: first total({{lo}}, {{mid}}), then total({{next}}, {{hi}}). Meanwhile this frame waits on the stack.
recursion-call-stack.combine: Both halves are back: {{left}} + {{right}} = {{result}}. total({{lo}}, {{hi}}) returns it and its frame pops.
recursion-call-stack.done: The sum is {{sum}}, after {{calls}} calls. The stack never held more frames than the tree is deep.

towers-of-hanoi.ready: Move {{n}} disks from peg 1 to peg 3, one at a time, never a bigger disk on a smaller one. It takes {{minimum}} moves.
towers-of-hanoi.call: hanoi({{n}}): to move {{n}} disks from {{source}} to {{target}}, first move the {{smaller}} smaller ones out of the way, to peg {{spare}}.
towers-of-hanoi.empty: hanoi(0): no disks to move, so it returns at once.
towers-of-hanoi.move: Move {{num}}: disk {{disk}} goes from peg {{source}} to peg {{target}}.
towers-of-hanoi.done: Done: {{moves}} moves (2ⁿ − 1 for n = {{n}}) and {{calls}} calls.
towers-of-hanoi.call_one: hanoi(1): a single disk, so move it straight from peg {{source}} to peg {{target}} (the calls with 0 disks around it just return).

bit-manipulation.ready: x = {{x}} and y = {{y}}, in binary. Each column is a power of two.
bit-manipulation.and: x & y = {{result}}: a 1 only where both x and y have a 1.
bit-manipulation.or: x | y = {{result}}: a 1 wherever x or y has a 1.
bit-manipulation.xor: x ^ y = {{result}}: a 1 where x and y differ.
bit-manipulation.left: x << 1 = {{result}}: every bit moves one place left, which doubles x.
bit-manipulation.right: x >> 1 = {{result}}: every bit moves one place right and the last one drops off: x halved, rounded down.
bit-manipulation.clear: {{before}} − 1 = {{minus}} flips the lowest 1 bit and the 0s below it, so {{before}} & {{minus}} = {{after}} clears just that bit. Count: {{num}}.
bit-manipulation.count: x reached 0: {{x}} has {{num}} bits set to 1. The loop ran once per 1 bit, not once per bit.
bit-manipulation.done: Done: {{ops}} bit operations, each a single machine step.

prefix-sums.ready: Build the prefix sums of {{n}} values: p[i] is the sum of everything left of position i, so p[0] = 0.
prefix-sums.query: Sum of positions {{lo}} to {{hi}}: p[{{upper}}] − p[{{lo}}] = {{top}} − {{bottom}} = {{answer}}. Two reads, whatever the range's length.
prefix-sums.done: {{additions}} additions built the row once; from now on every range sum costs one subtraction. This one is {{answer}}.

dynamic-array.ready: Append {{n}} values to an array that starts with room for one.
dynamic-array.room: size {{size}} < capacity {{capacity}}: there is room for {{v}}.
dynamic-array.full: size {{size}} = capacity {{capacity}}: full. Allocate new storage for {{bigger}} and copy everything across before adding {{v}}.
dynamic-array.copy: Copy a[{{i}}] = {{value}} into the new storage ({{copies}} copies so far).
dynamic-array.done: {{n}} appends cost {{copies}} copies in all: about {{cost}} writes per append. Doubling keeps that below 3, however many values arrive.

selection-sort.ready: Each pass finds the smallest value left and swaps it to the front of the unsorted part.
selection-sort.start: Pass {{i}}: assume a[{{i}}] = {{value}} is the smallest so far.
selection-sort.compare_smaller: Is {{value}} smaller than {{min}}? Yes: remember it as the new smallest.
selection-sort.new_min: The smallest so far is now {{value}}, at position {{at}}.
selection-sort.swap: Swap the smallest value, {{value}}, into position {{i}}: it is in its final place.
selection-sort.stay: {{value}} is already at position {{i}}: the swap changes nothing.
selection-sort.done: Sorted: {{comparisons}} comparisons and {{moves}} swaps for {{n}} values. The comparisons never depend on the order.

shell-sort.ready: Insertion sort over values a gap apart, with the gap halving each pass: far moves first, fine moves last ({{n}} values).
shell-sort.gap: Gap {{gap}}: sort every chain of values {{gap}} apart.
shell-sort.take: Lift {{key}} out of position {{i}} as the key.
shell-sort.compare_bigger: Is {{value}}, {{gap}} places to the left, bigger than {{key}}? Yes: it jumps right.
shell-sort.compare_stop: Is {{value}}, {{gap}} places to the left, bigger than {{key}}? No: the key stops here.
shell-sort.shift: Move {{value}} from position {{from}} to {{to}}; the gap moves left.
shell-sort.done: Sorted: {{comparisons}} comparisons and {{moves}} shifts for {{n}} values.

merge-sort.ready: Split the {{n}} values in halves until each part holds one value, then merge sorted halves back together.
merge-sort.copy: Both halves of {{lo}}–{{hi}} are sorted. Copy them into the buffer to merge them.
merge-sort.pick_left: Left head {{left}} ≤ right head {{right}}: the left one goes next (left first on ties keeps the sort stable).
merge-sort.pick_right: Right head {{right}} < left head {{left}}: the right one goes next.
merge-sort.left_only: The right half is used up: the left head {{left}} goes next.
merge-sort.right_only: The left half is used up: the right head {{right}} goes next.
merge-sort.done: Sorted: {{comparisons}} comparisons and {{writes}} writes for {{n}} values.

quick-sort-3way.ready: Quick sort with three parts: smaller than the pivot, equal to it, bigger. Equal values are finished in one pass.
quick-sort-3way.pivot: Sort {{lo}}–{{hi}}: the pivot is the first value, {{pivot}}.
quick-sort-3way.compare_less: {{value}} < {{pivot}}: it belongs to the smaller part.
quick-sort-3way.compare_greater: {{value}} > {{pivot}}: it belongs to the bigger part.
quick-sort-3way.less: Swap {{value}} to position {{lt}}, at the end of the smaller part; lt and i move on.
quick-sort-3way.greater: Swap {{value}} to position {{gt}}, at the front of the bigger part; gt moves back and i stays to check what came in.
quick-sort-3way.equal: {{value}} stays in the equal block; i moves on.
quick-sort-3way.done: Sorted: {{comparisons}} comparisons and {{moves}} swaps for {{n}} values.

heap-sort.ready: Arrange the {{n}} values as a max-heap (every parent ≥ its children), then take the biggest out again and again.
heap-sort.build: Sift down the parent at position {{start}} ({{value}}), so the subtree below it is a heap.
heap-sort.pick: The bigger child is {{child}}, at position {{at}}.
heap-sort.pick_only: There is one child: {{child}}, at position {{at}}.
heap-sort.compare_stop: Parent {{parent}} ≥ child {{child}}: this part is a heap; stop.
heap-sort.swap: {{up}} moves up and {{down}} moves down; keep sifting from its new place.
heap-sort.heap_ready: The heap is built: the biggest value, {{max}}, is at the root.
heap-sort.extract: Swap the root {{max}} to position {{end}}, its final place; the heap shrinks by one.
heap-sort.done: Sorted: {{comparisons}} comparisons and {{moves}} swaps for {{n}} values.

counting-sort.ready: {{n}} whole numbers from 0 to {{max}}: one bucket per value, so no value is compared with another.
counting-sort.count: {{v}} goes into bucket {{v}}, which now holds {{num}}.
counting-sort.write: Bucket {{v}} hands out a {{v}}: write it at position {{k}} ({{left}} left in the bucket).
counting-sort.done: Sorted with {{n}} counts and {{n}} writes, over {{buckets}} buckets.

radix-sort.ready: Sort {{n}} values up to {{max}} one digit at a time, from the ones up, with ten buckets per pass.
radix-sort.pass: New pass: sort by the digit worth {{place}}.
radix-sort.distribute: {{v}} has digit {{digit}} in the {{place}}s place: it goes to bucket {{digit}}.
radix-sort.collect: Take {{v}} out of bucket {{digit}} and write it at position {{k}}. Buckets keep their arrival order.
radix-sort.done: Sorted after {{passes}} passes over {{n}} values, without comparing two values.

bucket-sort.ready: Scatter {{n}} values into {{num}} buckets by range, sort each bucket, and read the buckets in order.
bucket-sort.scatter: {{v}} falls in the range {{range}}: into that bucket.
bucket-sort.sort: Sort bucket {{range}}: {{size}} value(s), a quick job.
bucket-sort.sort_empty: Bucket {{range}} is empty: nothing to sort.

tim-sort.ready: A simplified Tim sort: insertion sort makes runs of {{run}}, then runs are merged in pairs ({{n}} values).
tim-sort.run: Sort the run {{lo}}–{{hi}} with insertion sort.
tim-sort.take: Lift {{key}} out of position {{i}} as the key.
tim-sort.compare_bigger: Is {{value}} bigger than the key {{key}}? Yes: it shifts right.
tim-sort.compare_stop: Is {{value}} bigger than the key {{key}}? No: the key goes right after it.
tim-sort.merge: Merge the sorted runs {{lo}}–{{mid}} and the run after it, up to {{hi}} (width {{width}}).
tim-sort.pick_left: Left head {{left}} ≤ right head {{right}}: the left one goes next.
tim-sort.pick_right: Right head {{right}} < left head {{left}}: the right one goes next.
tim-sort.left_only: The right run is used up: {{left}} goes next.
tim-sort.right_only: The left run is used up: {{right}} goes next.
tim-sort.done: Sorted: {{comparisons}} comparisons and {{writes}} writes for {{n}} values.

quickselect.ready: Find the {{k}}-th smallest of {{n}} values: it is the value that would land at position k − 1 if the array were sorted.
quickselect.compare_smaller: Is {{value}} smaller than the pivot {{pivot}}? Yes: it joins the smaller part.
quickselect.compare_not: Is {{value}} smaller than the pivot {{pivot}}? No: it stays.
quickselect.swap: Swap {{value}} to position {{i}}, the end of the smaller part.
quickselect.swap_self: {{value}} is already at position {{i}}: the smaller part grows by one.
quickselect.place: The pivot {{pivot}} goes to position {{i}}, its final place.
quickselect.found: The pivot landed at position {{p}} = k − 1: it is the answer, {{value}}.
quickselect.go_right: The pivot is at {{p}}, left of {{want}}: search only the right side.
quickselect.go_left: The pivot is at {{p}}, right of {{want}}: search only the left side.
quickselect.done: The {{k}}-th smallest value is {{value}}, found with {{comparisons}} comparisons and only part of the array sorted.

linear-search.ready: Look for {{target}} among {{n}} values, one position at a time.
linear-search.missing: {{target}} is not here: all {{checks}} values checked.

binary-search.ready: Look for {{target}} in {{n}} sorted values by halving the range each time.
binary-search.mid: Range {{lo}}–{{hi}}: the middle is position {{mid}}, holding {{value}}.
binary-search.found: {{target}} is at position {{mid}}: found after {{checks}} checks.
binary-search.go_right: {{value}} < {{target}}: the target can only be to the right. Now lo = {{lo}}.
binary-search.go_left: {{value}} > {{target}}: the target can only be to the left. Now hi = {{hi}}.
binary-search.missing: The range is empty: {{target}} is not here ({{checks}} checks).

lower-upper-bound.ready: Find where {{target}} starts and ends among {{n}} sorted values, with two binary searches.
lower-upper-bound.lower_right: a[{{mid}}] = {{value}} < {{target}}: the first value ≥ {{target}} is further right.
lower-upper-bound.lower_left: a[{{mid}}] = {{value}} ≥ {{target}}: position {{mid}} may be the answer; keep the left half including it.
lower-upper-bound.lower_done: Lower bound = {{lower}}: the first position whose value is ≥ {{target}} ({{n}} if none).
lower-upper-bound.upper_right: a[{{mid}}] = {{value}} ≤ {{target}}: the first value > {{target}} is further right.
lower-upper-bound.upper_left: a[{{mid}}] = {{value}} > {{target}}: position {{mid}} may be the answer; keep the left half including it.
lower-upper-bound.upper_done: Upper bound = {{upper}}: the first position whose value is > {{target}} ({{n}} if none).
lower-upper-bound.done: {{target}} appears {{num}} time(s): positions {{lower}} up to, not including, {{upper}}.

binary-search-answer.ready: Ship {{n}} parcels in order within {{days}} days. The smallest daily capacity is between {{lo}} (the heaviest parcel) and {{hi}} (all of them).
binary-search-answer.fits: With capacity {{mid}} it takes {{need}} day(s) ≤ {{days}}: it fits, so the answer is {{mid}} or less.
binary-search-answer.too_small: With capacity {{mid}} it takes {{need}} days > {{days}}: too small, so the answer is more than {{mid}}.
binary-search-answer.answer: The smallest capacity is {{capacity}}: {{need}} day(s), after {{tries}} tries.

exponential-search.ready: Look for {{target}} in {{n}} sorted values: first find a range by doubling, then binary search inside it.
exponential-search.first_no: a[0] = {{value}} is not {{target}}: start doubling from 1.
exponential-search.double: a[{{bound}}] = {{value}} < {{target}}: the target is further on; double to {{next}}.
exponential-search.stop: a[{{bound}}] = {{value}} ≥ {{target}}: the target is before this bound.
exponential-search.range: The target can only be in {{lo}}–{{hi}}: binary search there.
exponential-search.found: {{target}} is at position {{mid}}: found after {{checks}} checks.

two-pointers.ready: Find two values that add up to {{target}} among {{n}} sorted values: one pointer at each end.
two-pointers.found: Positions {{i}} and {{j}} add up to {{total}}: found.
two-pointers.move_i: {{total}} < {{target}}: too small. {{value}} cannot be in any pair that fits, so i moves right.
two-pointers.move_j: {{total}} > {{target}}: too big. {{value}} cannot be in any pair that fits, so j moves left.
two-pointers.missing: The pointers met: no pair adds up to {{target}} ({{checks}} sums).

sliding-window.ready: Find the longest run of values with a sum of at most {{limit}}, among {{n}} positive values.
sliding-window.grow: Take in {{value}}: the window sum is {{total}} (limit {{limit}}).
sliding-window.shrink: Over the limit: drop {{value}} from the left; the sum is {{total}}.
sliding-window.best: The window {{lo}}–{{hi}} has {{length}} values: the best so far.
sliding-window.not_best: The window has {{length}} values; the best is still {{best}}.
sliding-window.done: The longest run has {{best}} values, starting at position {{start}}. The edges moved {{moves}} times for {{n}} values.

monotonic-stack.ready: For each of the {{n}} values, find the next value to its right that is bigger (−1 if none).
monotonic-stack.compare_pop: The top of the stack, {{top}} at position {{at}}, is smaller than {{value}}: {{value}} is its answer.
monotonic-stack.compare_stop: The top of the stack, {{top}}, is not smaller than {{value}}: stop popping.
monotonic-stack.pop: Pop position {{at}}: the next greater value after {{value}} is {{answer}}.
monotonic-stack.push: Push position {{at}} ({{value}}): it waits for a bigger value. The stack holds {{size}}.
monotonic-stack.done: Done: {{pops}} values got an answer; {{left}} still on the stack have none (−1).

stack.ready: Run {{n}} operations on an empty stack. Only the top is ever touched.
stack.push: push {{value}}: it goes on top. The stack holds {{size}}.
stack.pop: pop: take the top value, {{value}}, off. {{size}} left.
stack.pop_empty: pop on an empty stack: nothing to take, so the answer is −1.
stack.peek: peek: the top is {{value}}; it stays on the stack.
stack.done: Done. The output row holds the {{num}} values returned, in order.

queue-ring-buffer.ready: A queue in a fixed array of {{capacity}} slots. head is the front; the tail is head + size, wrapping around.
queue-ring-buffer.full: enqueue {{value}}: all {{capacity}} slots are full, so it is refused.
queue-ring-buffer.enqueue: enqueue {{value}}: write it at the tail, slot {{at}}.
queue-ring-buffer.dequeue: dequeue: take {{value}} from slot {{at}}; head moves on to {{head}} (wrapping at the end).
queue-ring-buffer.done: Done: {{num}} dequeues. Nothing was ever shifted: only head and tail moved.

deque-monotonic-queue.ready: Find the maximum of every window of {{k}} values among {{n}}. The deque keeps positions whose values decrease from front to back.
deque-monotonic-queue.pop_back: {{value}} (position {{at}}) ≤ {{by}}: it can never be a window's maximum again, so pop it off the back.
deque-monotonic-queue.pop_front: Position {{at}} ({{value}}) has left the window: pop it off the front.
deque-monotonic-queue.emit: Window {{lo}}–{{hi}}: its maximum is the front, {{max}}.
deque-monotonic-queue.done: {{windows}} window maxima with only {{pops}} pops in all: each position enters and leaves the deque once.

singly-linked-list.ready: Run {{n}} operations on an empty singly linked list. Each node knows only the next one.
singly-linked-list.link: front {{value}}: the new node points at the current head.
singly-linked-list.new_head: head now points at {{value}}: added in O(1).
singly-linked-list.first: back {{value}}: the list is empty, so the node becomes the head.
singly-linked-list.walk: Walk to the next node, {{value}}, looking for the last one.
singly-linked-list.append: {{after}} is the last node: link it to {{value}}. Reaching the back took a walk: O(n).
singly-linked-list.search: delete {{value}}: {{seen}} is not it, so prev and cur move on.
singly-linked-list.unlink_head: {{value}} is the head: head skips to the next node.
singly-linked-list.unlink: Found {{value}}: {{prev}} now links past it, and the node drops out.
singly-linked-list.not_found: delete {{value}}: the walk reached the end without finding it.
singly-linked-list.done: Done: the list holds {{size}} values, read from head to the end.

doubly-linked-list.ready: Run {{n}} operations on a doubly linked list: every node links forward and back, so both ends are O(1).
doubly-linked-list.link_front: front {{value}}: link it before the head, both ways. It is the new head.
doubly-linked-list.link_back: back {{value}}: link it after the tail, both ways. It is the new tail.
doubly-linked-list.unlink_front: pop-front: {{value}} leaves; the next node becomes the head and forgets its back link.
doubly-linked-list.unlink_back: pop-back: {{value}} leaves; the previous node becomes the tail. No walk needed.
doubly-linked-list.done: Done: {{pops}} pops; the list holds {{size}} values. The output reads it forwards and then backwards.

reverse-list.ready: Reverse a list of {{n}} nodes in place: walk once, turning every arrow around.
reverse-list.save: Save cur's next ({{next}}) as nxt before the link is overwritten.
reverse-list.new_head: cur ran off the end: prev, {{head}}, is the new head. {{n}} links flipped, no extra memory.

floyd-cycle.ready: {{n}} nodes; the last one links to position {{pos}} (−1 means no link). Does the list loop?
floyd-cycle.meet: slow and fast meet at node {{at}}: there is a cycle.
floyd-cycle.no_cycle: fast reached the end after {{steps}} moves: no cycle.
floyd-cycle.reset: Send slow back to the head; fast stays. Now both move 1 node at a time.
floyd-cycle.found: They meet at node {{at}} ({{value}}): that is where the cycle starts.

lru-cache.ready: An LRU cache holding at most {{capacity}} keys. Least recently used on the left, most recent on the right.
lru-cache.miss: get {{key}}: not in the cache (a miss), so −1.
lru-cache.hit: get {{key}}: a hit, value {{value}}. It moves to the most recent end.
lru-cache.refresh: put {{key}}: already cached, so move it to the most recent end first.
lru-cache.put: put {{key}} = {{value}} at the most recent end.
lru-cache.evict: Over capacity ({{capacity}}): evict the least recently used key, {{key}}.
lru-cache.done: Done: the output holds the {{gets}} answers to get.

dynamic-array-ops.ready: Run {{n}} operations on a dynamic array. Inserting or deleting in the middle moves every value after it.
dynamic-array-ops.grow: The array is full ({{size}} values): double the storage to {{capacity}} first.
dynamic-array-ops.shift_right: Shift {{value}} from position {{from}} to {{to}} to open a gap.
dynamic-array-ops.write: Write {{value}} into the gap at position {{at}}.
dynamic-array-ops.shift_left: {{removed}} is gone: shift {{value}} from position {{from}} to {{to}}.
dynamic-array-ops.shrink: The last slot is now spare: {{size}} values remain.
dynamic-array-ops.empty: remove on an empty array: nothing to do.
dynamic-array-ops.done: Done: {{size}} values, after {{shifts}} shifts in all. Work at the end is cheap; in the middle it costs a shift per value after it.

separate-chaining.ready: Insert {{n}} keys into a table of {{m}} buckets. Each bucket is a list.
separate-chaining.scan_empty: Bucket {{b}} is empty: nothing to compare.
separate-chaining.scan: Scan bucket {{b}} ({{len}} key(s)) for {{key}}: not there.
separate-chaining.duplicate: {{key}} is already in bucket {{b}}: skip it.
separate-chaining.insert: Append {{key}} to bucket {{b}}, which now holds {{len}}.
separate-chaining.done: {{n}} keys stored; the longest chain has {{longest}}. Short chains keep lookups fast.

open-addressing.ready: A table of {{m}} slots, one key each. Collisions move on to the next slot (linear probing).
open-addressing.hash: Key {{key}}: its home slot is {{key}} mod 8 = {{home}}.
open-addressing.probe: The slot holds {{was}}, not {{key}}: try the next one, slot {{slot}}.
open-addressing.not_found: Slot {{slot}} is empty: {{key}} is not in the table (0).
open-addressing.tombstone: Delete {{key}}: leave a tombstone ✕ in slot {{slot}}, so later searches keep probing past it.
open-addressing.delete_missing: {{key}} is not in the table: nothing to delete.
open-addressing.done: Done: {{finds}} find(s), {{probes}} probe(s) past occupied slots.

bloom-filter.ready: A Bloom filter: {{m}} bits and three hash functions. It answers "maybe" or "definitely not".
bloom-filter.check_set: check {{key}}: bit {{p}} is set; look at the next one.
bloom-filter.check_clear: check {{key}}: bit {{p}} is clear, so {{key}} was never added.
bloom-filter.maybe: All of {{key}}'s bits ({{positions}}) are set: maybe (1). Other keys may have set them.
bloom-filter.done: Done: {{checks}} check(s). A "no" is always right; a "maybe" can be a false positive.

rolling-hash.ready: Hash every window of {{length}} letters in a {{n}}-letter text: base {{base}}, mod {{mod}}.
rolling-hash.shift_in: Shift and add {{letter}} ({{code}}): h = {{h}}, the next window's hash.
rolling-hash.done: {{windows}} window hashes, each in O(1) after the first window, however long the window ({{length}}).

tree-traversals.ready: The {{n}} values form a binary search tree. Visit it in three orders.
tree-traversals.in: In-order: write {{value}} between its children (#{{k}}). A BST comes out sorted.
tree-traversals.done: Each order visited all {{n}} nodes once: O(n).

level-order.ready: Visit the tree of {{n}} values level by level, starting with the root, {{root}}.
level-order.visit: Take {{value}} from the front of the queue and write it.
level-order.done: Every one of the {{n}} nodes came out in level order.

bst-operations.ready: Run {{n}} operations on an empty binary search tree: smaller keys go left, the rest right.
bst-operations.descend_right: insert {{value}}: not smaller than {{at}}, go right.
bst-operations.root: The tree is empty: {{value}} becomes the root.
bst-operations.not_found: find {{value}}: fell off the tree, not found (0).
bst-operations.splice: {{value}} has at most one child: its child takes its place.
bst-operations.successor: Two children: look for the successor, the smallest key on the right. Go left to {{at}}.
bst-operations.copy: Copy the successor {{from}} over {{was}}, then delete the successor below.
bst-operations.done: Done. The output holds the find answers, 0, then the {{size}} keys in order.

binary-heap.ready: Run {{n}} operations on a min-heap: every parent is at most its children, so the root is the smallest.
binary-heap.append: push {{value}}: add it at the end, position {{at}}.
binary-heap.compare_up_stop: {{value}} is not smaller than its parent {{parent}}: it stays.
binary-heap.compare_up_swap: {{value}} is smaller than its parent {{parent}}: sift it up.
binary-heap.take: pop: the root, {{value}}, is the smallest. Take it.
binary-heap.move_last: Move the last value, {{value}}, to the root.
binary-heap.compare_down_stop: {{value}} is not bigger than its smaller child {{child}}: the heap is in order.
binary-heap.compare_down_swap: {{value}} is bigger than its smaller child {{child}}: sift it down.
binary-heap.done: Done: {{pops}} pop(s), {{size}} value(s) left. Each push and pop touched one path: O(log n).

trie.ready: Insert {{n}} words into a trie, then count the words that start with "{{prefix}}".
trie.new_node: No edge for {{letter}} yet: add a node for "{{path}}".
trie.follow: Follow {{letter}}; {{num}} word(s) now pass through this node.
trie.missing: No edge for {{letter}}: no word starts with "{{prefix}}".
trie.count_word: {{num}} word(s) start with "{{prefix}}", and "{{prefix}}" is a word itself.
trie.count_only: {{num}} word(s) start with "{{prefix}}"; it is not a whole word.

union-find.ready: {{n}} elements, each in a set of its own: every element is its own root.
union-find.compress: Point {{node}} straight at the root {{root}}, so the next find is shorter.
union-find.same: union {{a}} {{b}}: both are already under root {{root}}.
union-find.link: Link root {{child}} under root {{root}} (the bigger set); it now holds {{size}}.

tree-diameter.ready: A tree of {{n}} nodes. Find its longest path, counting edges.
tree-diameter.first_bfs: First BFS from node 0: the farthest node it reaches is one end of a longest path.
tree-diameter.visit: Visit node {{node}} at distance {{d}}; the farthest so far is {{best}}.
tree-diameter.second_bfs: Node {{end}} was the farthest (distance {{d}}). Second BFS from there.
tree-diameter.done: The farthest node from {{a}} is {{b}}: the diameter is {{length}} edge(s).

avl-rotations.ready: Insert {{n}} values into an AVL tree. Under each node: its height h and its balance (left height − right height).
avl-rotations.place: Place {{value}} as a new leaf, as in any binary search tree.
avl-rotations.balanced: Back at {{value}}: balance {{balance}}, within −1 to +1. Nothing to fix.
avl-rotations.left_heavy: Back at {{value}}: balance {{balance}}. The left side is two levels taller: rotate.
avl-rotations.right_heavy: Back at {{value}}: balance {{balance}}. The right side is two levels taller: rotate.
avl-rotations.rotate_right: Rotate right: {{top}} moves up, {{down}} becomes its right child.
avl-rotations.rotate_left: Rotate left: {{top}} moves up, {{down}} becomes its left child.
avl-rotations.done: {{n}} values, height {{height}}, after {{rotations}} rotation(s). The pre-order is the output.

red-black-insert.ready: Insert {{n}} values into a left-leaning red-black tree. A red node is glued to its parent; red links only lean left.
red-black-insert.place: Place {{value}} as a new red leaf.
red-black-insert.rotate_left: A red link leans right: rotate left, {{top}} moves up over {{down}}.
red-black-insert.rotate_right: Two red links in a row on the left: rotate right, {{top}} moves up over {{down}}.
red-black-insert.flip: {{value}} has two red children: flip the colours, so {{value}} turns red and passes the red up.
red-black-insert.done: {{n}} values after {{rotations}} rotation(s). Every path from the root down meets {{black}} black node(s).

b-tree-insert.ready: Insert {{n}} values into a B-tree where a node holds at most {{max}} keys.
b-tree-insert.descend: {{key}} goes below this node, into child {{child}}.
b-tree-insert.add_key: Add {{key}} to the leaf, keeping its keys in order.
b-tree-insert.split: Too many keys: split around the middle key {{middle}}, which moves up.
b-tree-insert.absorb: The parent takes {{middle}} and now points to both halves.
b-tree-insert.new_root: The root split: {{middle}} becomes a new root, and the tree grows one level taller.
b-tree-insert.done: {{n}} values, height {{height}}, after {{splits}} split(s). Every leaf is at the same depth.

segment-tree.ready: {{n}} values in a segment tree of {{nodes}} nodes. Each node stores the sum of the range under it.
segment-tree.merge: Range {{lo}}-{{hi}}: its sum is its two children added, {{sum}}.
segment-tree.outside: Range {{lo}}-{{hi}} is fully outside the query: skip it.
segment-tree.inside: Range {{lo}}-{{hi}} is fully inside: take its {{sum}} without going lower. Total so far {{acc}}.
segment-tree.update: update {{i}} {{value}}: walk down to the leaf.
segment-tree.done: {{answers}} answer(s), {{visited}} nodes visited by the queries.

lazy-propagation.ready: {{n}} zeros in a segment tree with lazy tags. Under each node: its range and its pending tag.
lazy-propagation.tag: Range {{lo}}-{{hi}} is fully inside: add {{value}} for each position (sum {{sum}}) and leave a tag for the children.
lazy-propagation.push_down: Range {{lo}}-{{hi}} must go lower: pass its tag +{{tag}} to both children first.
lazy-propagation.recompute: Range {{lo}}-{{hi}}: recompute its sum from its children, {{sum}}.
lazy-propagation.inside: Range {{lo}}-{{hi}} is fully inside: take its {{sum}}. Total so far {{acc}}.
lazy-propagation.done: {{answers}} answer(s); tags were passed down {{pushes}} time(s).

fenwick-tree.ready: {{n}} zeros in a Fenwick tree. Slot i covers the positions shown under it.
fenwick-tree.start_add: add {{i}} {{value}}: every slot that covers position {{i}} needs {{value}} more.
fenwick-tree.add: Slot {{slot}} now holds {{total}}. Next slot: add its lowest bit, {{low}}.
fenwick-tree.start_sum: sum {{i}}: add the slots that together cover positions 0 to {{i}}.
fenwick-tree.read: Read slot {{slot}} ({{value}}): total {{acc}}. Then drop its lowest bit.
fenwick-tree.done: {{answers}} answer(s): {{reads}} slot reads and {{writes}} slot writes in all.

lca-binary-lifting.ready: A tree of {{n}} nodes. Build a table of jumps: each node's ancestor 1, 2, 4… levels up ({{levels}} level(s)).
lca-binary-lifting.table: {{jump}} level(s) above {{v}}: two jumps of half that, via {{mid}}, land on {{to}}.
lca-binary-lifting.lift: Lift the deeper node {{from}} by {{jump}} to {{to}}.
lca-binary-lifting.same: Same depth and the same node: {{lca}} is the answer for {{a}} and {{b}}.
lca-binary-lifting.jump: Jump {{jump}} up from {{from_a}} and {{from_b}}: they land on different nodes, {{a}} and {{b}}, so keep the jump.
lca-binary-lifting.answer: No jump keeps them apart any more: their parent {{lca}} is the answer for {{a}} and {{b}}.

graph-representations.ready: {{n}} nodes and {{m}} edges. Build an adjacency list and an adjacency matrix in one pass.
graph-representations.matrix: Write its weight {{w}} in row {{u}}, column {{v}}.
graph-representations.list_back: Undirected: also add {{u}} to {{v}}'s list and write {{w}} in row {{v}}, column {{u}}.
graph-representations.done: The list holds {{list}} entries; the matrix always has {{cells}} cells, edges or not.

bfs.ready: Breadth-first search from node 0 over {{n}} nodes. The number under a node is its distance in edges.
bfs.visit: Take {{u}} from the front of the queue (distance {{d}}).
bfs.discover: {{v}} is new: distance {{d}}, one more than {{u}}. It joins the back of the queue.
bfs.seen: {{v}} already has a distance ({{d}}): skip it.
bfs.done: {{reached}} of {{n}} nodes reached; the farthest is {{far}} edge(s) away.

dfs.ready: Depth-first search from node 0 over {{n}} nodes. The number under a node is the order it was entered.
dfs.go: {{v}} is unseen: go deeper, from {{u}} to {{v}}.
dfs.seen: {{v}} was already seen: try {{u}}'s next neighbour.
dfs.leave: {{u}} has no unseen neighbours left: it is finished, back up.
dfs.done: {{reached}} of {{n}} nodes reached. The output is the entry order, then the finish order.

cycle-detection.ready: Look for a cycle among {{n}} nodes and directed edges. Every node starts white.
cycle-detection.grey: Enter {{u}}: it turns grey, on the current path.
cycle-detection.black_edge: {{u}} → {{v}}: {{v}} is black, already finished. No cycle through it.
cycle-detection.back_edge: {{u}} → {{v}}: {{v}} is grey, still on the path. This edge closes a cycle.
cycle-detection.black: {{u}} has no more edges to follow: it turns black.
cycle-detection.cycle: A cycle exists: the answer is 1.
cycle-detection.no_cycle: All {{n}} nodes are black and no edge went back up a path: no cycle, the answer is 0.

topological-sort.ready: {{n}} nodes; under each, its in-degree (edges coming in). {{free}} node(s) have none and wait in the queue.
topological-sort.take: Take {{u}}: nothing still points to it, so it can go next.
topological-sort.lower: Remove {{u}} → {{v}}: {{v}} now has {{d}} edge(s) coming in.
topological-sort.ready_node: {{v}} has no edges coming in: it joins the queue.
topological-sort.done: All {{n}} nodes are in order: every edge points forward.
topological-sort.stuck: The queue is empty but {{left}} node(s) remain: they are on a cycle, so no order exists for them.

connected-components.ready: Find the connected pieces among {{n}} nodes. The label under a node is its component.
connected-components.new: {{s}} has no label yet: start component #{{c}} there.
connected-components.pop: Pop {{u}} from the stack and look at its neighbours.
connected-components.fill: {{v}} gets label #{{c}} too, from {{u}}, and goes on the stack.

bipartite-check.ready: Try to split {{n}} nodes into two sides, A and B, so that every edge goes across.
bipartite-check.start: {{s}} has no side yet: put it on side A and spread from there.
bipartite-check.colour: {{v}}, a neighbour of {{u}}, goes on the other side.
bipartite-check.fine: {{u}} and {{v}} are on different sides: fine.
bipartite-check.clash: {{u}} and {{v}} are on the same side but share an edge: there is an odd cycle, no split exists.
bipartite-check.done: Every edge goes across: {{a}} node(s) on side A, {{b}} on side B.

dijkstra.ready: Shortest distances from node 0 over {{n}} nodes; the number under a node is its best distance so far.
dijkstra.pop: Pop the smallest entry: {{u}} at distance {{d}}.
dijkstra.stale: This entry ({{d}}) is older than {{u}}'s best ({{best}}): skip it.
dijkstra.relax: Through {{u}}, {{v}} costs {{d}} (edge {{w}}): better, so update it and push it.
dijkstra.no_better: Through {{u}}, {{v}} would cost {{via}}: not better than {{best}}.
dijkstra.done: The queue is empty: {{reached}} of {{n}} nodes reached, each with its shortest distance.

bellman-ford.ready: Shortest distances from node 0 with {{m}} directed edges, some negative: at most {{rounds}} round(s).
bellman-ford.round: Round {{round}} of {{of}}: try every edge in order.
bellman-ford.settled: Round {{round}} changed nothing: the distances are final.
bellman-ford.check: One more pass: if any edge still lowers a distance, there is a negative cycle.
bellman-ford.negative_cycle: {{u}} → {{v}} (weight {{w}}) still lowers a distance: a negative cycle is reachable, so the answer is 1.
bellman-ford.done: No edge lowers anything: the distances are final after {{relaxed}} update(s) and {{checked}} edge checks.

floyd-warshall.ready: {{n}} nodes, {{m}} directed edges. The matrix starts with the direct edges; ∞ means no path yet.
floyd-warshall.pivot: Now allow paths through node {{k}}: row {{k}} and column {{k}} are the ways in and out.
floyd-warshall.improve_new: {{i}} → {{k}} → {{j}} costs {{d}}: the first path from {{i}} to {{j}}.
floyd-warshall.done: Every node has been a middle stop: the matrix holds all shortest distances ({{checks}} checks, {{improved}} improvements).

zero-one-bfs.ready: Distances from node 0 over {{n}} nodes; every edge weighs 0 or 1. A deque replaces the priority queue.
zero-one-bfs.front: {{u}} → {{v}} is free: {{v}} gets {{d}} and goes to the front.
zero-one-bfs.back: {{u}} → {{v}} costs 1: {{v}} gets {{d}} and goes to the back.

prim.ready: Grow a minimum spanning tree from node 0 over {{n}} nodes. The queue holds (weight·node) for edges leaving the tree.
prim.pop: Pop the cheapest entry: node {{v}} for {{w}}.
prim.skip: {{v}} is already in the tree: skip this entry.
prim.push: Edge {{u}} – {{v}} ({{w}}) now leaves the tree: push it.
prim.done: The tree spans {{size}} of {{n}} nodes and weighs {{total}}.

kruskal.ready: Sort the {{m}} edges by weight and take each one that joins two different trees.
kruskal.consider: Next cheapest: {{u}} – {{v}} ({{w}}). Find both ends' roots.
kruskal.skip: {{u}} and {{v}} are already in one tree (root {{root}}): this edge would close a cycle.
kruskal.join: Different trees: take {{u}} – {{v}} and merge them. Total {{total}}.
kruskal.done: {{taken}} edge(s) taken, total weight {{total}}, across {{n}} nodes.

scc.ready: Find the strongly connected components of {{n}} nodes: groups where every node can reach every other.
scc.finish: Pass 1: {{u}} is finished, number {{k}} in the finish order.
scc.reverse: Pass 2: reverse every edge, then start from the last node to finish.
scc.start: {{u}} has no component yet: start component #{{c}} there.

bridges-articulation.ready: Find the bridges and cut vertices of {{n}} nodes. Under each node: its entry number / its low value.
bridges-articulation.back: {{u}} – {{v}} goes back up to number {{t}}: {{u}}'s low becomes {{low}}.
bridges-articulation.bridge: {{v}}'s subtree reaches no higher than {{low}}, below {{u}} ({{t}}): {{u}} – {{v}} is a bridge.
bridges-articulation.cut: {{v}}'s subtree cannot get above {{u}} (low {{low}} ≥ {{t}}): {{u}} is a cut vertex.
bridges-articulation.root_cut: The root {{u}} has {{children}} separate subtrees: it is a cut vertex.

max-flow.ready: Send as much as possible from node {{source}} to node {{sink}}. Each edge shows flow / capacity.
max-flow.search: Look for a path with spare capacity (current flow {{flow}}).
max-flow.path: Found a path of {{len}} edge(s); its bottleneck is {{push}}.
max-flow.augment: Push {{push}} along {{u}} → {{v}}, and allow {{push}} back the other way.
max-flow.done: No path with spare capacity is left: the maximum flow is {{flow}} ({{paths}} path(s)).

eulerian-path.ready: Draw all {{m}} edges in one stroke? {{odd}} node(s) have an odd degree.
eulerian-path.odd: {{odd}} odd-degree nodes: a path needs 0 or 2, so there is none.
eulerian-path.back: {{u}} has no unused edges: move it to the path.
eulerian-path.done: All {{m}} edges used once, from {{start}} to {{end}}.
eulerian-path.missed: {{left}} edge(s) were never reached: the graph is in pieces, so there is no path.

grid-bfs.ready: Find the fewest steps from S to G on a {{rows}} × {{cols}} grid. Every step costs 1.
grid-bfs.visit: Take ({{r}}, {{c}}) from the queue: {{d}} step(s) from S.
grid-bfs.discover: ({{r}}, {{c}}) is new: {{d}} step(s) from S. It joins the back of the queue.
grid-bfs.goal: G reached in {{d}} step(s), after exploring {{explored}} cell(s).
grid-bfs.done: The shortest path takes {{d}} step(s); {{explored}} cell(s) were explored.
grid-bfs.no_path: The queue is empty after {{explored}} cell(s): walls cut G off.

grid-dijkstra.ready: Find the cheapest path from S to G on a {{rows}} × {{cols}} grid. Entering a cell costs its weight (1 when open).
grid-dijkstra.stale: ({{r}}, {{c}}) already has {{best}}: this entry ({{d}}) is stale, skip it.
grid-dijkstra.relax: Through here, ({{r}}, {{c}}) costs {{d}}: better, so update it and push it.
grid-dijkstra.goal: G is settled at cost {{d}}, after exploring {{explored}} cell(s).
grid-dijkstra.done: The cheapest path costs {{d}}; {{explored}} cell(s) were explored.
grid-dijkstra.no_path: The queue is empty after {{explored}} cell(s): walls cut G off.

a-star.ready: A* from S to G on a {{rows}} × {{cols}} grid: the queue orders cells by f = g (cost so far) + h (Manhattan distance to G).
a-star.pop: Pop the smallest f: ({{r}}, {{c}}) with g = {{d}}.
a-star.stale: ({{r}}, {{c}}) already has g = {{best}}: this entry is stale, skip it.
a-star.goal: G is popped with cost {{d}}, after exploring {{explored}} cell(s).
a-star.done: The cheapest path costs {{d}}; only {{explored}} cell(s) were explored.
a-star.no_path: The queue is empty after {{explored}} cell(s): walls cut G off.

greedy-best-first.ready: Greedy best-first from S to G on a {{rows}} × {{cols}} grid: always expand the cell that looks closest to G.
greedy-best-first.pop: Pop the smallest h: ({{r}}, {{c}}), {{h}} away from G.
greedy-best-first.discover: ({{r}}, {{c}}) is new: h = {{h}}, paid {{d}} so far. Push it.
greedy-best-first.goal: G reached at cost {{d}}, after exploring {{explored}} cell(s). Fast, but not always the cheapest path.
greedy-best-first.done: The path found costs {{d}}; {{explored}} cell(s) were explored.
greedy-best-first.no_path: The queue is empty after {{explored}} cell(s): walls cut G off.

maze-generation.ready: Carve a {{size}} × {{size}} maze with {{cells}} rooms by randomized depth-first search (seed {{seed}}).
maze-generation.carve: {{options}} unvisited neighbour(s); the generator picks number {{pick}}. Knock down the wall and move to ({{r}}, {{c}}).
maze-generation.back: ({{r}}, {{c}}) is a dead end: back up one room.
maze-generation.done: All {{cells}} rooms are connected, with exactly one path between any two.

fibonacci-memo-table.ready: fib({{n}}) two ways: top-down with a memo, then bottom-up with a table.
fibonacci-memo-table.hit: fib({{k}}) is already in the memo: {{value}}. No more calls below it.
fibonacci-memo-table.store: fib({{k}}) = {{value}}: store it in the memo.
fibonacci-memo-table.table: The memo needed {{calls}} call(s). Now bottom-up: start the table with 0 and 1.
fibonacci-memo-table.done: fib({{n}}) = {{value}}: {{calls}} call(s) top-down, {{fills}} addition(s) bottom-up, and no repeated work either way.

climbing-stairs.ready: Ways to climb {{n}} steps, 1 or 2 at a time. ways[0] = 1: standing still.
climbing-stairs.one: Reach step {{i}} with a single step from {{from}}: {{ways}} way(s) so far.
climbing-stairs.two: Or with a double step from {{from}}: add {{add}}, {{ways}} way(s).

house-robber.ready: {{n}} houses in a row; neighbours cannot both be robbed.
house-robber.take: House {{house}}: taking it gives {{take}}, skipping gives {{skip}}. Take it.
house-robber.skip: House {{house}}: taking it gives {{take}}, skipping gives {{skip}}. Skip it.
house-robber.trace: Back from the end: house {{house}} ({{value}}) was taken.

maximum-subarray.ready: Find the run of {{n}} values with the biggest sum.
maximum-subarray.restart: The run so far is not positive, so it cannot help: start a new run at {{value}} (index {{i}}).
maximum-subarray.extend: Extend the run with {{value}}: its sum is {{current}}.
maximum-subarray.done: The best run sums to {{best}}, from index {{from}} to {{to}}.

coin-change.ready: Fewest coins for {{amount}} using {{kinds}} coin value(s), each as often as needed. ∞ means cannot be made.
coin-change.total: Total {{total}}: try ending with each coin.
coin-change.improve: End with a {{coin}}: fewest[{{from}}] + 1 = {{num}} coin(s), the best so far for {{total}}.
coin-change.impossible: {{amount}} cannot be made with these coins: the answer is -1.

knapsack-01.ready: {{n}} items, capacity {{capacity}}: each item is packed once or not at all. Row i uses the first i items.
knapsack-01.skip: Item {{item}} at capacity {{c}}: start without it, from the cell above: {{value}}.
knapsack-01.take: Item {{item}} at capacity {{c}}: packing it gives {{value}}, more than {{without}} without it.
knapsack-01.trace: Back from the corner: item {{item}} was packed (weight {{weight}}), {{left}} capacity left.

rod-cutting.ready: A rod of length {{n}}, and a price for every piece length. Pieces can repeat.
rod-cutting.length: Length {{length}}: try every length for the first piece.
rod-cutting.improve: First piece {{cut}}, then the best for {{rest}}: {{value}}, the best so far.
rod-cutting.done: A rod of {{n}} earns at most {{best}}, in {{num}} piece(s).

lis.ready: Find the longest strictly increasing subsequence of {{n}} values (not necessarily side by side).
lis.start: Value {{value}} at {{i}}: on its own, a run of 1.
lis.extend: {{a}} (at {{j}}) is smaller than {{b}}: extend its run to length {{length}}.
lis.done: The longest increasing subsequence has {{length}} value(s).

lcs.ready: Longest common subsequence of "{{a}}" and "{{b}}": letters in the same order, not necessarily side by side.
lcs.match: Both letters are "{{letter}}": one more than the diagonal, {{value}}.
lcs.carry: "{{x}}" ≠ "{{y}}": keep the better of above and left, {{value}}.
lcs.trace: Back from the corner: "{{letter}}" is in the common subsequence.
lcs.done: The longest common subsequence is "{{word}}" ({{length}} letter(s)).

edit-distance.ready: Fewest single-letter edits (insert, delete, replace) to turn "{{a}}" into "{{b}}". Row 0 and column 0: build from or to nothing.
edit-distance.same: Both letters are "{{letter}}": no edit needed, {{value}} as on the diagonal.
edit-distance.change: "{{x}}" ≠ "{{y}}": 1 + the cheapest of replace ({{replaced}}), delete ({{remove}}) and insert ({{insert}}) = {{value}}.

grid-paths.ready: Count the paths through a {{rows}} × {{cols}} grid moving only right or down; {{blocked}} cell(s) are blocked.
grid-paths.blocked: ({{r}}, {{c}}) is blocked: no path goes through it.
grid-paths.start: The top-left cell: one path, standing still.

word-break.ready: Can "{{text}}" be cut into the {{num}} dictionary word(s)?
word-break.end: Can the first {{end}} letters, "{{prefix}}", be cut?
word-break.fits: "{{word}}" ends here and letters before {{start}} can be cut: yes up to {{end}}.
word-break.none: No word ends at {{end}} after a good cut: no.
word-break.fail: No: "{{text}}" cannot be cut into dictionary words.

matrix-chain.ready: Multiply {{n}} matrices in a row with the fewest scalar multiplications: the order of the brackets matters, the result does not.
matrix-chain.split: Matrices {{i}}..{{j}} split after {{k}}: {{left}} + {{right}} + {{join}} = {{total}}, the best so far.

bitmask-tsp.ready: Shortest round trip from city 0 through all {{n}} cities. Each row is a set of visited cities written as bits ({{rows}} rows).
bitmask-tsp.extend: From {{last}} on to {{city}}: {{total}}, the best so far for the set {{set}} ending at {{city}}.
bitmask-tsp.close: All cities visited: go back from {{last}} to 0 (+{{back}}), {{total}} in all.
bitmask-tsp.done: The shortest round trip through {{n}} cities is {{total}}.

activity-selection.ready: {{n}} activities, one room: fit in as many as possible.
activity-selection.sorted: Sort them by end time: the one that ends first leaves the most room.
activity-selection.take: Activity {{k}} ({{start}}–{{end}}) starts after the room is free: take it.
activity-selection.clash: Activity {{k}} starts at {{start}}, but the room is busy until {{free}}: skip it.

merge-intervals.ready: Merge {{n}} intervals wherever they overlap or touch.
merge-intervals.open: {{start}}–{{end}} starts after the last merged interval ends: open a new one.
merge-intervals.extend: {{start}}–{{end}} overlaps the last merged interval: it now ends at {{to}}.

jump-game.ready: From each of {{n}} squares you may jump forward up to its number. Can you reach the last square?
jump-game.farther: Square {{i}} with a jump of {{jump}} reaches square {{reach}}: farther than before.
jump-game.stuck: Square {{i}} is beyond the farthest reach, {{reach}}: stuck.

fractional-knapsack.ready: {{n}} items that can be cut, a bag of {{capacity}}: carry the most value.
fractional-knapsack.sorted: Sort them by value per unit of weight, best first.
fractional-knapsack.take: Item {{k}} (weight {{w}}, value {{v}}) fits whole: {{total}} so far, {{room}} room left.
fractional-knapsack.part: Item {{k}} weighs {{w}} but only {{room}} is left: take {{room}}/{{w}} of it, worth {{num}}/{{den}}.
fractional-knapsack.done: The bag is full: {{whole}} + {{num}}/{{den}} in value.

huffman-coding.ready: Build a prefix code for {{n}} symbols: the more frequent a symbol, the shorter its code.
huffman-coding.merge: Join the two lightest trees, {{a}} and {{b}}, under a new node of {{sum}}.
huffman-coding.done: {{bits}} bits in all, against {{fixed}} with a fixed-length code.

subsets.ready: List all {{total}} subsets of {{n}} values: at each call, keep what is chosen, then try adding each later value.
subsets.undo: Take {{value}} back out and try the next value.
subsets.done: {{num}} subsets of {{n}} values: every value is either in or out.

permutations.ready: List every order of {{n}} values: fill the places one by one with any value not used yet.
permutations.undo: Take {{value}} back and try the next unused value.

combination-sum.ready: Every way to make {{target}} from {{n}} candidates, each usable many times, in non-decreasing order.
combination-sum.prune: {{value}} is more than the {{left}} left, and every later candidate is too: stop this branch.

n-queens.ready: Place {{n}} queens on a {{n}} × {{n}} board so that none attacks another: one per row, top to bottom.
n-queens.place: Row {{row}}: column {{col}} is not attacked, place a queen.
n-queens.dead_end: Row {{row}}: every column is attacked. Dead end: go back up.
n-queens.remove: Remove the queen from row {{row}}, column {{col}}, and try the next column.

sudoku.ready: Fill the {{size}} × {{size}} Sudoku: {{empty}} empty cell(s), first empty cell first, digits in order.
sudoku.place: Row {{row}}, column {{col}}: {{digit}} is not in its row, column or box yet. Try it.
sudoku.undo: Nothing fits further on: take {{digit}} back out of row {{row}}, column {{col}}.
sudoku.impossible: No digit fits somewhere whatever came before: this Sudoku has no solution.

word-search.ready: Find "{{word}}" in the {{rows}} × {{cols}} grid, moving up, down, left or right, never reusing a cell.
word-search.step: "{{letter}}" at ({{row}}, {{col}}): letter {{k}} matches, step onto it.
word-search.back: No way on from "{{letter}}" at ({{row}}, {{col}}): step back.

kmp.ready: Find "{{pattern}}" in "{{text}}". First the failure table: the longest border of each prefix.
kmp.fall: Mismatch at {{i}}: fall back to the shorter border, {{k}}.
kmp.border: fail[{{i}}] = {{k}}: the first {{k}} letter(s) also end here.
kmp.scan: Now scan the text; on a mismatch, slide the pattern to its border instead of starting over.
kmp.skip: "{{letter}}" at {{i}} does not match: keep {{k}} matched letter(s) from the border.
kmp.done: {{num}} match(es) with {{reads}} comparisons; the scan never moves back in the text.

z-function.ready: Search "{{pattern}}" in "{{text}}" with the Z-function of pattern | text.
z-function.reuse: {{i}} is inside the Z-box: start from z[{{from}}], {{value}}.
z-function.extend: One more letter agrees with the start: z[{{i}}] = {{value}}.
z-function.done: {{num}} match(es): wherever z equals the pattern's length.

rabin-karp.ready: The pattern's hash is {{target}}; the first window of {{m}} letter(s) hashes to {{window}}.
rabin-karp.window: Window at {{at}}: hash {{hash}} ≠ {{target}}, so no need to compare letters.
rabin-karp.match: Window at {{at}}: same hash {{hash}} and same letters. Match.
rabin-karp.collision: Window at {{at}}: same hash {{hash}} but different letters, a collision.

manacher.ready: Longest palindrome in "{{text}}": bars between the letters let one rule handle even and odd lengths.
manacher.mirror: {{i}} is inside the rightmost palindrome: its mirror {{mirror}} says at least {{value}}.
manacher.grow: The letters on both sides agree: radius {{value}} at {{i}}.
manacher.reach: The palindrome centred at {{center}} now reaches {{right}}.

aho-corasick.ready: Count {{num}} patterns in one pass over the text. First, a trie of the patterns.
aho-corasick.built: The trie has {{nodes}} node(s). Now the failure links, level by level.
aho-corasick.link: Node "{{letter}}" fails to "{{to}}": the longest suffix that is also in the trie.
aho-corasick.follow: No "{{letter}}" edge here: follow the failure link.

suffix-array.ready: Sort the {{n}} suffixes of "{{text}}". Start by ranking each by its first letter.
suffix-array.sort: Sort by the first {{two}} letters (rank of the first {{k}}, then of the next {{k}}): {{distinct}} different rank(s).
suffix-array.double: Ranks still tie: double the length to {{k}}.
suffix-array.done: All {{n}} suffixes are ordered after {{rounds}} round(s).

euclid-gcd.ready: Greatest common divisor of {{a}} and {{b}}: replace (a, b) by (b, a mod b) until b is 0.
euclid-gcd.divide: {{a}} mod {{b}} = {{rest}}: any divisor of both also divides the rest.
euclid-gcd.done: b is 0: the GCD is {{gcd}}, found in {{steps}} division(s).

fast-power.ready: {{base}}^{{exp}} mod {{mod}}: square the base once per bit of the exponent, multiply it in where the bit is 1.
fast-power.square: Square the base for the next bit: {{base}}.

modular-inverse.ready: Find x with {{a}} · x ≡ 1 (mod {{m}}) by the extended Euclidean algorithm.
modular-inverse.divide: Quotient {{q}}: the next remainder is {{r}}, with coefficient {{x}}.
modular-inverse.none: {{a}} and {{m}} share the factor {{g}}: there is no inverse.

pascal-ncr.ready: Build Pascal's triangle down to row {{n}}: each entry is the sum of the two above it.
pascal-ncr.done: Row {{n}} holds C({{n}}, k) for every k; together they sum to {{sum}}.

sieve-eratosthenes.ready: Find the primes up to {{n}}: cross out the multiples of each prime.
sieve-eratosthenes.prime: {{p}} is still open, so it is prime: cross out its multiples from {{start}} (smaller ones are already gone).
sieve-eratosthenes.again: {{m}} was already crossed out by a smaller prime.

convex-hull.ready: Wrap the {{n}} points in the smallest convex fence.
convex-hull.sorted: Sort the {{n}} distinct points left to right; build the lower chain first.
convex-hull.drop: A right turn (or a straight line) at ({{x}}, {{y}}): it is inside, drop it.
convex-hull.upper: Lower chain done. Now the upper chain, right to left.

segment-intersection.ready: Do segments P1P2 and P3P4 meet? Check on which side of each segment the other's ends lie.
segment-intersection.cross: Each segment's ends lie on opposite sides of the other: they cross.
segment-intersection.touch: {{point}} lies on the other segment: they touch.
segment-intersection.apart: No crossing and no touching: the segments are apart.
